'''Christina Pagel''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|p|aː|ɡ|ə|l}} {{respell|PAH|gəl}}) '''FMedSci HonFFPH''' is a German-British mathematician and professor of [[Operations research|operational research]] at [[University College London]] (UCL) within UCL's Clinical Operational Research Unit (CORU),<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=|date=2018-12-18|title=The Team|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/clinical-operational-research-unit/team|access-date=2022-02-09|website=Clinical Operational Research Unit|language=en}}</ref> which applies operational research, data analysis and mathematical modelling to topics in healthcare. She was Director of UCL CORU from 2017 to 2022<ref>{{cite tweet |user=chrischirp |number=1542488807966113792 |date=30 June 2022 |title=Personal news: after 5 yrs, today's my last day as Director of @UCL_CORU. |author=Christina Pagel}}</ref> and is currently Vice President of the UK [[Operational Research Society]].<ref name="OR">{{Cite web|title=Board Members|url=https://www.theorsociety.com/about-us/board/|access-date=2022-02-09|website=The OR Society}}</ref> She also co-leads, alongside [[Rebecca Shipley]], UCL's CHIMERA research hub which analyses data from critically ill hospital patients.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|date=2020-07-17|title=Our team|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/chimera/our-team|access-date=2022-02-09|website=CHIMERA|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Pagel graduated with a BA in mathematics from [[The Queen's College, Oxford]] in 1996. She also holds an MSc in Mathematical Physics from [[King's College London]], and MAs in Classical Civilisation, Medieval History and an MSc in Applied Statistics with Medical Applications from [[Birkbeck, University of London|Birkbeck College]], University of London. In 2002 Pagel was awarded a PhD in Space Physics on ''Turbulence in the [[interplanetary magnetic field]]'' from [[Imperial College London]].<ref name="Iris">{{Cite web|title=Iris View Profile|url=https://iris.ucl.ac.uk/iris/browse/profile?upi=ACPAG88|access-date=2021-10-07|website=UCL}}</ref>

== Research ==
Pagel's early career was spent in [[Boston]], Massachusetts, studying the scattering of electrons in interplanetary space using data from the [[Advanced Composition Explorer|ACE spacecraft]] at Boston University with Professor [[Nancy Crooker]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pagel|first1=C.|last2=Crooker|first2=N. U.|last3=Larson|first3=D. E.|last4=Kahler|first4=S. W.|last5=Owens|first5=M. J.|year=2005|title=Understanding electron heat flux signatures in the solar wind|journal=Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics|volume=110|issue=A1|article-number=2004JA010767 |doi=10.1029/2004JA010767|bibcode=2005JGRA..110.1103P |issn=2156-2202|url=http://centaur.reading.ac.uk/5835/1/2005%20Pagel%20et%20al%2C%202005%20JGR%202004JA010767.pdf|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2005 she left physics, returning to London to take up a position with the UCL Clinical Operational Research Unit applying mathematics to problems in health care.

In 2016, Pagel was awarded a [[Harkness Fellowship]] in Health Care Policy and Practice by the [[Commonwealth Fund]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/mathematical-physical-sciences/news/2016/feb/christina-pagel-wins-prestigious-harkness-fellowship|title=Christina Pagel wins prestigious Harkness Fellowship|last=UCL|date=1 February 2016|website=UCL Mathematical & Physical Sciences|access-date=5 October 2019}}</ref> through which Pagel spent 2016–2017 in the USA researching (a) the priorities of Republican and Democrat politicians for the goals of national health policy working with the [[Milbank Memorial Fund]] and (b) how clinical decision support systems can be better implemented within intensive care settings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.commonwealthfund.org/person/christina-pagel|title=Christina Pagel {{!}} Commonwealth Fund|website=www.commonwealthfund.org|access-date=6 October 2019}}</ref> During that year, she also completed a fellowship at the [[Institute for Healthcare Improvement]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ihi.org:80/Engage/Fellowships/Pages/alumni.aspx|title=Fellowship Alumni|website=ihi.org|access-date=9 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pagel|first1=Christina|last2=Ramnarayan|first2=Padmanabhan|last3=Ray|first3=Samiran|last4=Peters|first4=Mark J.|date=1 February 2018|title=Development and implementation of a real time statistical control method to identify the start and end of the winter surge in demand for paediatric intensive care|journal=European Journal of Operational Research|volume=264|issue=3|pages=847–858|doi=10.1016/j.ejor.2016.08.023|issn=0377-2217|url=https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1505952/|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Pagel was appointed as director of UCL's Clinical Operational Research Unit (CORU) in 2017.<ref name=":2" /> Her research uses approaches from mathematical modelling, operational research and data sciences to help people within the health service make better decisions.<ref name="Iris" /> She focuses on mortality and morbidity outcomes following [[cardiac surgery]] in children and adults in the UK, leading and contributing to several large national projects;<ref>{{Cite In her role since 2020 at UCL's CHIMERA centre (Collaborative Healthcare Innovation through Mathematics, EngineeRing and AI), Pagel co-leads a multidisciplinary team which analyses anonymised data from intensive care patients at [[University College Hospital]] and [[Great Ormond Street Hospital]]. Using tools including [[machine learning]], the centre aims to improve understanding of the physiology of patients during illness and recovery, in order to improve their care.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|title=CHIMERA|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/chimera/|access-date=2022-02-09|website=University College London|date=22 July 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

Pagel was instrumental in developing a [[statistical model]] to take into account the complexity of individual children with [[Congenital heart defect|congenital heart disease]], when considering a hospital's survival rate. This led to the Partial Risk Adjustment in Surgery (PRAiS) model, which has been used by the National Congenital Heart Disease Audit since 2013 to publish hospital survival rates,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hqip.org.uk/resource/national-congenital-heart-disease-audit-2013-2016/|title=National Congenital Heart Disease Audit 2013 – 2016|date=8 March 2018|website=HQIP|access-date=16 October 2019}}</ref> and the associated software, developed by Pagel, has been purchased by all UK hospitals performing children's heart surgery.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://xip.uclb.com/i/software/clinical_data_modelling/PRAiS.html|title=XIP: PRAiS v3|website=XIP, online licensing portal|access-date=5 October 2019}}</ref> She then led a multidisciplinary project<ref name=":0" /> working with the Children's Heart Federation, [[Sense about Science]] and [[David Spiegelhalter|Sir David Spiegelhalter]] to build a website on survival after children's heart == Outreach and public engagement ==
Pagel is active in school and university [[Science outreach|outreach]], encouraging participation in mathematics and science subjects.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ima.org.uk/10273/ima-early-career-mathematicians-autumn-conference-2018/|title=IMA Early Career Mathematicians' Autumn Conference 2018|date=18 September 2018|website=IMA|access-date=9 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bbk.ac.uk/annual-events/mathematical-sciences-seminar|title=Mathematical Sciences Seminar – Birkbeck, University of London|website=bbk.ac.uk|access-date=9 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chinaplatetheatre.com/were-stuck|title=We're Stuck! {{!}} China Plate Theatre|website=www.chinaplatetheatre.com|access-date=9 October 2019|archive-date=9 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191009215947/https://www.chinaplatetheatre.com/were-stuck}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://imascientist.org.uk/2013/05/whos-taking-part-in-june-2013/|title=I'm a Scientist, Get me out of here! 2013 participants|date=9 October 2019|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130805073247/http://imascientist.org.uk/2013/05/whos-taking-part-in-june-2013 |archive-date=5 August 2013 }}</ref>

Her work in developing the children's heart surgery website formed the basis of a national guide for researchers on how to involve the public<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://senseaboutscience.org/activities/public-engagement-guide/|title=Public engagement: a practical guide – Sense about Science|website=senseaboutscience.org|date=6 November 2017 |access-date=9 October 2019}}</ref> and was separately featured in a [[Health Foundation]] guide on engagement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.health.org.uk/publications/section-3-extending-influence-and-widening-impact|title=Section 3: Extending influence and widening impact|publisher=The Health Foundation|access-date=9 October 2019}}</ref>

She also contributed to the Sense about Science guide "Making Sense of Statistics".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://senseaboutscience.org/activities/making-sense-of-statistics/|title=Making Sense of Statistics – Sense about Science|website=senseaboutscience.org|date=29 April 2010 |access-date=9 October 2019}}</ref>

In 2023, she was the Mathematics Section President for the annual British Science Festival.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2023-05-11 |title=17 of the UK's best scientific minds announced as Scientific Section Presidents |url=https://www.britishscienceassociation.org/News/17-of-the-uks-best-scientific-minds-announced-as-scientific-section-presidents |access-date=2023-06-01 |website=British Science Association |language=en}}</ref>

Since November 2024, Pagel has been writing regularly about the [[Donald Trump|Trump]] Administration, covering its attacks on science, health and democratic norms more broadly.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pagel |first=Christina |title=US politics {{!}} Diving into Data & Decision making {{!}} Christina Pagel {{!}} Substack |url=https://christinapagel.substack.com/ |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=christinapagel.substack.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pagel |first1=Christina |last2=Buse |first2=Kent |last3=McKee |first3=Martin |date=2024-11-28 |title=Evidence abandoned: Trump's cabinet and the fallout for science |url=https://www.bmj.com/content/387/bmj.q2654 |journal=BMJ |language=en |volume=387 |article-number=q2654 |doi=10.1136/bmj.q2654 |issn=1756-1833 |pmid=39608840|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Christina Pagel |url=https://politicalquarterly.org.uk/authors/christina-pagel/ |access-date=2025-07-22 |website=Political Quarterly |language=en}}</ref> She launched the [https://www.trumpactiontracker.info/? TrumpActionTracker] website in July 2025, which keeps track of authoritarian-like actions of the administration since January 2025.

==Awards and recognition==
In 2019, Pagel was awarded the [[Operational Research Society#Awards|Lyn Thomas Impact Medal]] from the [[Operational Research Society]], along with her colleagues Sonya Crowe and Martin Utley. The award was made for their work related to [[Congenital heart defect|congenital heart disease]] and recognised the "significant impact on the lives of children with congenital heart disease, as well on their families and the growing population of adults with the condition".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lyn Thomas Medal Winners – The OR Society|url=https://www.theorsociety.com/what-we-do/awards-medals-and-scholarships/lyn-thomas-impact-medal/lyn-thomas-medal-winners/|access-date=22 December 2019|website=theorsociety.com}}</ref>

In September 2021, Pagel was one of two recipients (alongside [[Devi Sridhar]]) of a special recognition award from ''[[The BMJ]]'', and in October 2021 she won a [[HealthWatch|HealthWatch UK]] award, both for her work in public engagement in science during the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jones|first=Helen|date=2021-09-30|title=The BMJ Awards 2021: Special recognition award for science communication|url=https://www.bmj.com/content/374/bmj.n2326|journal=BMJ|language=en|volume=374|article-number=n2326|doi=10.1136/bmj.n2326|issn=1756-1833|pmid=34593375|s2cid=238219978 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Winners 2021|url=https://thebmjawards.bmj.com/winners-2021/|access-date=2021-10-07|website=The BMJ Awards|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Award - HealthWatch-UK|url=https://www.healthwatch-uk.org/awards.html|access-date=2021-10-14|website=www.healthwatch-uk.org}}</ref> She was a Turing Fellow of the [[Alan Turing Institute]] by special appointment from 2021 to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|last=UCL|date=2020-10-28|title=Turing people at UCL|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/alan-turing-institute/turing-people-ucl|access-date=2021-11-04|website=UCL and The Turing|language=en}}</ref> In November 2021, she was awarded the "Companion of OR" prize by the UK [[Operational Research Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Companion of OR - The OR Society|url=https://www.theorsociety.com/membership/awards-medals-and-scholarships/companion-of-or/|access-date=2021-11-15|website=www.theorsociety.com}}</ref>

She was appointed as Vice President of the UK Operational Research Society for a three-year period from January 2022 to December 2024, and extended for a second term (2025-2027). She delivered the prestigious annual Blackett Lecture in December 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blackett Lecture - The OR Society |url=https://www.theorsociety.com/events/blackett-lecture/ |access-date=2022-12-16 |website=www.theorsociety.com}}</ref><ref name="OR" />

In 2023 she was named as the Mathematics Section President for the annual [[British Science Association|British Science Festival]]. Presidents are considered leaders in their fields.<ref name=":3" />

She was a [[Royal Statistical Society]] 2023 "Statistical Excellence in Journalism Award" winner, in the category "Best statistical commentary by a non-journalist" for her article '' "Physics: Do girls avoid it because it's too hard?"'' –  [[BBC Science Focus]], 9 May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statistical Excellence in Journalism Awards: 2023 winners |url=https://rss.org.uk/news-publication/news-publications/2023/general-news/statistical-excellence-in-journalism-award-2023-wi/ |access-date=2023-07-07 |website=RSS}}</ref>

Pagel was elected as an Honorary Fellow of the UK [[Faculty of Public Health]] (FPH) in 2024, the highest category of FPH membership<ref>{{Cite web|title=FPH welcomes ten new Honorary Fellows |url=https://www.fph.org.uk/news/fph-welcomes-ten-new-honorary-fellows/ |access-date=2024-07-01 |publisher=Faculty of Public Health |language=en}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences (United Kingdom)|Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=UCL |date=2025-05-22 |title=Seven UCL academics elected to the Academy of Medical Sciences |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/2025/may/seven-ucl-academics-elected-academy-medical-sciences |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=UCL News |language=en}}</ref>
